name: OUTPUT -> REPLAY -> NULL -> STATISTIC -> CALIBRATION
question: Given a preserved output of a dead experiment, does the statistic it reported survive a matched null and a calibrated floor, without re-running the organism?

steps.does: census the preserved ledger: rows, malformed lines, dead fields, verdict columns, time range
instrument-null the historical statistic: TAUTOLOGICAL / NONDETERMINISTIC / RESPONSIVE before any replay is read
block-shuffle null preserving within-stratum structure (or NT-008 permutation null / NT-049 random-subset null as the design dictates)
matched-null p with floor 1/(n+1); Holm-Bonferroni across the family
certify that the battery catches every named defect shape; NT-002 to separate B1 from B2 when the answer is 'nothing'

output_contract: per-claim row {historical_value, instrument_null_reading, null_quantile, p_floor, p_corrected, certifier_verdict, coverage_verdict}; a claim whose step-2 reading is TAUTOLOGICAL stops at step 2 with verdict INSTRUMENT_CANNOT_SEE and no p is reported
